title: One Van for the Valley
transcript: Three orchards in the same valley used to send separate vans to shops in town. Each van made nearly the same trip with plenty of space left inside. The growers agreed to load a single vehicle at the orchard closest to the main road. Their first shared delivery ran late because the driver had to open several crates to work out which fruit belonged to which shop. After that, growers attached a destination card to every crate before bringing it to the loading point. They divided the delivery charge according to the space each orchard used, which helped smaller growers keep sending modest orders during the quiet weeks.

questions.prompt: What made the growers' original delivery arrangement inefficient?
options: The shops ordered at widely different times.
The vans could only take one kind of fruit.
The route required several trips back to each orchard.
Several vans covered similar routes with room to spare.
questions.answer: Several vans covered similar routes with room to spare.
questions.explanation: 各果园的货车走的路线几乎相同，但车里都留有大量空余空间。

questions.prompt: Why did the charging system suit growers with modest orders?
options: They could pay after the shops sold their fruit.
They received a discount for delivering during quiet weeks.
Their share of the charge reflected the room their crates took up.
Their regular deliveries earned them priority on the route.
questions.answer: Their share of the charge reflected the room their crates took up.
questions.explanation: 运费按各果园占用的车内空间分摊，货量少的果园也能继续发送小批订单。
